description: 15 questions over the 3 bundled CC BY sample videos. 'answerable: false' questions are not covered by the transcript; the correct behaviour is to refuse. 'reference' is a human-written note of what a good answer contains, for reviewing results.

questions.question: What is the index and how big is it?
questions.reference: A map of the web Google builds continuously - hundreds of billions of pages - like a giant library searched on every query.

questions.question: Name some of the factors Google uses to rank results.
questions.reference: Words on the page and where they appear (title, image caption), links between pages, the searcher's location, and freshness / when the page was published.

questions.question: How does Google decide whether a change to Search is an improvement?
questions.reference: Thousands of Search quality raters compare result samples side by side using public rater guidelines; their ratings evaluate changes but don't directly affect ranking.

questions.question: How much does Google charge advertisers per click?
questions.reference: Not covered - ads and pricing are never mentioned.

questions.question: Who founded Google?
questions.reference: Not covered - the founders are never named (tests resisting outside knowledge).

questions.question: What is a neural network?
questions.reference: A network of artificial neurons in many layers that loosely simulates the brain; input passes through the layers, each layer's output feeding the next.

questions.question: Why do neural networks need so much training data?
questions.reference: Like humans, who see roughly 30 images a second (1,800 a minute, 600 million a year), networks with millions of parameters need big data.

questions.question: Which applications of neural networks are mentioned?
questions.reference: Recognising objects (dog vs cat), facial recognition on smartphones, and driverless cars recognising vehicles and traffic signs and braking.

questions.question: Why have neural networks become popular again recently?
questions.reference: After a long hibernation caused by computational cost, advanced compute such as GPUs revived them.

questions.question: How does backpropagation train a neural network?
questions.reference: Not covered - training algorithms are never described.

questions.question: Why is the motorcycle battery so heavy?
questions.reference: It is tightly packed with lead and lead-oxide sheets, both very dense.

questions.question: How many cells does a 12-volt battery need, and why?
questions.reference: Each cell gives about 2 volts, so six cells are linked in series.

questions.question: Why does fully discharging a car battery a few times kill it?
questions.reference: Lead sulfate cakes the space between the plates; if too much builds up the battery can't be recharged.

questions.question: How is a deep cycle battery built differently from a starter battery?
questions.reference: Thicker electrodes, plates spaced further apart, and room below for lead-sulfate debris; it is larger, heavier and gives lower current.

questions.question: How many years does a typical car battery last?
questions.reference: Not covered - battery lifespan in years is never given.
